newsitem.title: GERMANY: Prodi has talks with Tietmeyer in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: Prodi has talks with Tietmeyer in Frankfurt.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, visiting Germany as part of efforts to ensure Italy will not be excluded from European monetary union in 1999, held private talks with Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer in Frankfurt on Monday.
Tietmeyer, who in the past has been sceptical about whether Mediterranean countries have the track record to ensure a stable single currency, declined to make any substantial comment on the talks.
"It was a private talk and we had a good conversation," he told reporters.

The discussion took place at the headquarters of Commerzbank on the fringes of a dinner with bankers and business leaders including Commerzbank management board chairman Martin Kohlhaussen, German bourse chairman Werner Seifert and Degussa management board chairman Uwe-Ernst Bufe.
